key_insight: When partial checks reliably identify failures but cannot confirm correctness, suppressing verified negatives avoids directly rewarding false positives.
engineering_relevance: NOPO offers a policy-training approach for settings where unit tests, constraint checks, or LLM verifiers can reject failures but cannot certify successful solutions.
method: Treat non-falsified responses as unlabeled rather than correct.
Apply a reference-relative loss to suppress trusted verified negatives.
Scale each update by the group’s proportion of non-falsified responses.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved pass@k over baselines on code, logic, and math benchmarks, with gains persisting under inference-time scaling and cross-benchmark transfer.
watch_item: NOPO assumes verified negatives are reliable; erroneous failure labels could suppress valid solutions.
paper_title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards
